title: The canonical morphism Spec O_{Y,y} -> Y is flat and identifies local rings
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $y\in Y$, $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ its local ring [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and $Y'=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with closed point $y'=\mathfrak m$. The *canonical morphism* $c:Y'\to Y$ is the morphism of schemes corresponding to the pair $(y,\mathrm{id}_A)$ (the identity map $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to A$) under the bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring]: for any affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq Y$ containing $y$, with $y$ the prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, the natural map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is an isomorphism and $c$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(R_{\mathfrak p})\to\operatorname{Spec}R=V\subseteq Y$, independent of $V$. Then: (1) $c(y')=y$, and the image $c(Y')$ is the set of generalizations of $y$; in particular $c(Y')\subseteq V$ for every open $V\ni y$, i.e. $c^{-1}(V)=Y'$. (2) For every $q\in Y'$ the local homomorphism $c^\sharp_q:\mathcal O_{Y,c(q)}\to\mathcal O_{Y',q}$ induced by $c$ [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism] is an isomorphism; for $q=y'$ it is the identity of $A$ under $\mathcal O_{Y',y'}=A_{\mathfrak m}=A$. (3) Consequently $c$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. (4) For every $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal G$ with pullback $c^*\mathcal G$ [def-pc-module-pullback], the map $\mathcal G_y\to(c^*\mathcal G)_{y'}$ sending the germ of $s\in\mathcal G(V)$ to the germ at $y'$ of the image of $s$ under the unit $\mathcal G\to c_*c^*\mathcal G$ (a section of $c^*\mathcal G$ over $c^{-1}(V)=Y'$) is an isomorphism of $A$-modules (the stalk $(c^*\mathcal G)_{y'}$ is $\mathcal G_y\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\mathcal O_{Y',y'}$ and $c^\sharp_{y'}$ is the identity). (5) For every ideal $J\subsetneq A$ (so that $A/J$ is a local ring and the quotient map is a local homomorphism), the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)\to Y$ induced by $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to A/J$ (the one corresponding to the pair $(y,\mathcal O_{Y,y}=A\to A/J)$ under [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring]) is $c$ composed with the closed immersion $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)\to Y'$ given by the quotient map.

proof.text: (Construction through an affine open.) Choose an affine open $V\subseteq Y$ with $y\in V$ ([lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] with $W=Y$), put $R=\mathcal O_Y(V)$, let $\iota_V:\operatorname{Spec}R\to Y$ be the canonical open immersion with image $V$ and $\mathfrak p\subset R$ the prime with $\iota_V(\mathfrak p)=y$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] (c) the germ map $\gamma_V:R\to A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $r\mapsto r_y$, is a localization of $R$ at $R\setminus\mathfrak p$, so $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A$, $r/s\mapsto r_ys_y^{-1}$, is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; this is the natural isomorphism $R_{\mathfrak p}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ of the statement. Put $c_V=\iota_V\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma_V):\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Since $\gamma_V$ is the composite of $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$ with the isomorphism $R_{\mathfrak p}\cong A$, contravariant functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ shows that $c_V$ is the composite $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(R_{\mathfrak p})\to\operatorname{Spec}R\xrightarrow{\iota_V}Y$ of the statement. Every affine open $V\ni y$ may be used here.

source.place: Schemes, proof of Lemma 01J6 (lemma-morphism-from-spec-local-ring), affine case, and proof of Lemma 01J7 (lemma-specialize-points): $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_{X,x})=\operatorname{Spec}(R_{\mathfrak p})\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)=U\subset X$

proof.text: (Independence of $V$.) Let $V_1,V_2$ be affine opens containing $y$, $R_i=\mathcal O_Y(V_i)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] (applied to the open $V_1\cap V_2\ni y$) there is an affine open $W$ with $y\in W\subseteq V_1\cap V_2$; put $T=\mathcal O_Y(W)$ and let $\rho_i:R_i\to T$ be the restriction maps. The germ at $y$ of a section equals the germ of its restriction [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], so $\gamma_{V_i}=\gamma_W\circ\rho_i$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma_{V_i})=\operatorname{Spec}(\rho_i)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma_W)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; and $\iota_{V_i}\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\rho_i)=\iota_W$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-inclusion-spec-map] (as $W\subseteq V_i$). Hence $c_{V_i}=\iota_{V_i}\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\rho_i)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma_W)=\iota_W\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma_W)=c_W$ for $i=1,2$, and $c_{V_1}=c_{V_2}$. Call this morphism $c$, and fix from now on one affine open $V\ni y$ with $R$, $\mathfrak p$, $\gamma=\gamma_V$ as in Step 1, so that $c=\iota_V\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$. (That $c$ corresponds to the pair $(y,\mathrm{id}_A)$ is shown in Step 5; Stacks obtains the independence from the uniqueness in 01J6, which this comparison makes explicit.)

source.place: Schemes, Equation 02NA (equation-canonical-morphism) and the proof of Lemma 01J6 (lemma-morphism-from-spec-local-ring): the morphism does not depend on the affine open chosen

proof.text:
(Clause (1).) By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] (1) for $\lambda=\gamma$ and $W=R\setminus\mathfrak p$, $Q\mapsto\gamma^{-1}(Q)$ is a bijection from the primes of $A$ onto the primes $\mathfrak q\subset R$ with $\mathfrak q\cap(R\setminus\mathfrak p)=\emptyset$, i.e. $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$, with inverse $\mathfrak q\mapsto\mathfrak qA$; and $\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ maps the point $Q$ to $\gamma^{-1}(Q)$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-residue-field-naturality] (1). So $\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)(Y')=\{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}R:\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p\}$. The closed point: $\mathfrak pA$ is a prime of $A$ with $\gamma^{-1}(\mathfrak pA)=\mathfrak p$, and $\mathfrak pA\subseteq\mathfrak m$ ($\mathfrak m$ the unique maximal ideal), so $\mathfrak p=\gamma^{-1}(\mathfrak pA)\subseteq\gamma^{-1}(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak p$; hence $\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)(y')=\mathfrak p$ and $c(y')=\iota_V(\mathfrak p)=y$. The image: in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ the closure of $\{\mathfrak q\}$ is $V(\mathfrak q)=\{\mathfrak q'\supseteq\mathfrak q\}$ (Zariski topology [def-weil-affine-spectrum]), so $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ if and only if $\mathfrak q$ is a generalization of $\mathfrak p$. As $\iota_V$ is a homeomorphism onto the open subset $V$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points], [def-weil-open-immersion], it maps the generalizations of $\mathfrak p$ onto the points $x\in V$ with $y\in\overline{\{x\}}\cap V$ (the closure in the subspace $V$ is the closure in $Y$ intersected with $V$), i.e. onto the generalizations of $y$ lying in $V$. Finally every generalization $x$ of $y$ lies in every open $V'
i y$: otherwise $x$ lies in the closed set $Y\setminus V'$, hence so does $\overline{\{x\}}
i y$, a contradiction. Therefore $c(Y')=\iota_V(\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)(Y'))$ is exactly the set of generalizations of $y$, and $c(Y')\subseteq V'$, i.e. $c^{-1}(V')=Y'$, for every open $V'
i y$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01J7 (lemma-specialize-points) and its proof; the last paragraph of the proof of Lemma 01J6 (an open containing the closed point is everything)

proof.text: (Clause (2): the stalk maps are isomorphisms.) Let $q\in Y'$ with prime $Q\subset A$ and $\mathfrak q=\gamma^{-1}(Q)$, so $\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)(q)=\mathfrak q$ (Step 3) and $x:=c(q)=\iota_V(\mathfrak q)\in V$; as $\iota_V$ is injective, $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak p_x$ is the prime of $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-stalk-map-composition] (b) applied to $c=\iota_V\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, $c^\sharp_q=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)^\sharp_Q\circ\iota^\sharp_{V,\mathfrak q}$ with $\iota^\sharp_{V,\mathfrak q}:\mathcal O_{Y,x}\to\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathfrak q}$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)^\sharp_Q:\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathfrak q}\to\mathcal O_{Y',q}$. The first is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] (b). By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization], under the identifications $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathfrak q}\cong R_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\mathcal O_{Y',q}\cong A_Q$ given by the germ maps of global sections [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field] (1), the second is $\gamma_Q:R_{\mathfrak q}\to A_Q$, $r/s\mapsto\gamma(r)/\gamma(s)$, which is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] (2). So $c^\sharp_q$ is a composite of two ring isomorphisms, hence an isomorphism (and local, an isomorphism of local rings carrying the maximal ideal onto the maximal ideal).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 02OD (lemma-formal-functions-stalk): 'a flat morphism as it identifies local rings'; the identification is written out here from Schemes 01J7's description $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_{X,x})=\operatorname{Spec}(R_{\mathfrak p})\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$

proof.text: (Clause (2) at $y'$, and $c$ is the morphism of 02NA.) Let $\varepsilon:A\to\mathcal O_{Y',y'}$ be the germ at $y'$ of global sections of $Y'=\operatorname{Spec}A$; it is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring] (a), the identification $\mathcal O_{Y',y'}=A_{\mathfrak m}=A$ of the statement. Let $r\in R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] (b), $\iota^\sharp_{V,\mathfrak p}(r_y)$ is the germ of $r$ at $\mathfrak p$; by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization] (with $\psi=\gamma$, $Q=\mathfrak m$, $\gamma^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak p$ by Step 3), $\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)^\sharp_{y'}$ sends the germ of $r$ at $\mathfrak p$ to the germ of $\gamma(r)$ at $y'$, which is $\varepsilon(\gamma(r))=\varepsilon(r_y)$. With the factorization $c^\sharp_{y'}=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)^\sharp_{y'}\circ\iota^\sharp_{V,\mathfrak p}$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-stalk-map-composition] (b) this gives $c^\sharp_{y'}(r_y)=\varepsilon(r_y)$ for all $r\in R$. Every element of $A$ is $r_ys_y^{-1}$ with $r\in R$, $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ (Step 1), and ring homomorphisms preserve inverses, so $c^\sharp_{y'}=\varepsilon$, i.e. $\varepsilon^{-1}\circ c^\sharp_{y'}=\mathrm{id}_A$: under $\mathcal O_{Y',y'}=A$ the map $c^\sharp_{y'}$ is the identity of $A$. Together with $c(y')=y$ (Step 3) this says that $c$ corresponds to the pair $(y,\mathrm{id}_A)$ under the bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring] (b), as the statement asserts.

source.place: Schemes, Equation 02NA (equation-canonical-morphism): the canonical morphism corresponds to the identity map on the local ring under Lemma 01J6 (lemma-morphism-from-spec-local-ring)

proof.text: (Clause (3): flatness.) For every $q\in Y'$ the local homomorphism $c^\sharp_q:\mathcal O_{Y,c(q)}\to\mathcal O_{Y',q}$ is a ring isomorphism (Step 4). A ring isomorphism $\varphi:B\to C$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]: for every $B$-module $N$ the map $N\to N\otimes_BC$, $n\mapsto n\otimes1$, is an isomorphism, natural in $N$, with inverse $n\otimes c'\mapsto\varphi^{-1}(c')n$; so $-\otimes_BC$ carries injective maps to injective maps. Hence $\mathcal O_{Y',q}$ is a flat $\mathcal O_{Y,c(q)}$-module for every $q\in Y'$, i.e. $c$ is flat at every point, and $c$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 02OD (lemma-formal-functions-stalk): 'This is a flat morphism as it identifies local rings'

proof.text: (Clause (4): the stalk of the pullback.) Let $\mathcal G$ be an $\mathcal O_Y$-module, $V'\ni y$ open and $s\in\mathcal G(V')$, and let $c^*s\in(c^*\mathcal G)(c^{-1}V')=(c^*\mathcal G)(Y')$ (Step 3) be the image of $s$ under the unit $\mathcal G\to c_*c^*\mathcal G$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback] (for $f=c$ and the point $y'$, $c(y')=y$) there is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{Y',y'}$-modules $\beta:(c^*\mathcal G)_{y'}\to\mathcal G_y\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\mathcal O_{Y',y'}$, the tensor product formed with $c^\sharp_{y'}$, with $\beta((c^*s)_{y'})=s_y\otimes1$. Since $c^\sharp_{y'}$ is a ring isomorphism (Step 4), $\tau:\mathcal G_y\to\mathcal G_y\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\mathcal O_{Y',y'}$, $g\mapsto g\otimes1$, is bijective, with inverse $g\otimes b\mapsto(c^\sharp_{y'})^{-1}(b)\,g$ (well defined, the expression being bilinear and balanced; the composites are the identity on the elements $g$ and on the generators $g\otimes b=(c^\sharp_{y'})^{-1}(b)g\otimes1$). Every element of $\mathcal G_y$ is a germ $s_y$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], and the map of the statement, $s_y\mapsto(c^*s)_{y'}$, equals $\beta^{-1}\circ\tau$; so it is well defined and bijective. It is linear for $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ acting on $(c^*\mathcal G)_{y'}$ through $c^\sharp_{y'}$ ($\tau(ag)=ag\otimes1=g\otimes c^\sharp_{y'}(a)$), and $c^\sharp_{y'}=\varepsilon$ is the identification $A=\mathcal O_{Y',y'}$ (Step 5); hence it is an isomorphism of $A$-modules, and $(c^*\mathcal G)_{y'}=\mathcal G_y\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\mathcal O_{Y',y'}$ with $c^\sharp_{y'}$ the identity.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 0098 (lemma-stalk-pullback-modules), applied to $c$ at $y'$ with $c^\sharp_{y'}$ the identity

proof.text: (Clause (5).) Let $J\subsetneq A$ be an ideal and $\pi:A\to A/J$ the quotient map. Since $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$ and the ideals of $A/J$ are the $I/J$ with $J\subseteq I$, $A/J$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/J$, and $\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak m/J)=\mathfrak m$, so $\pi$ is a local homomorphism. $\operatorname{Spec}(\pi):\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)\to Y'$ is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-closed-immersion]. Put $h=c\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\pi)$ and let $z$ be the closed point $\mathfrak m/J$ of $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$. Then $\operatorname{Spec}(\pi)(z)=\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak m/J)=\mathfrak m=y'$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-residue-field-naturality] (1), so $h(z)=c(y')=y$ (Step 3). By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-stalk-map-composition] (b), $h^\sharp_z=\operatorname{Spec}(\pi)^\sharp_z\circ c^\sharp_{y'}$. Let $\varepsilon':A/J\to\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}(A/J),z}$ be the germ map of global sections, an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring] (a). By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization] (with $\psi=\pi$, $Q=\mathfrak m/J$), $\operatorname{Spec}(\pi)^\sharp_z\circ\varepsilon=\varepsilon'\circ\pi$, and $c^\sharp_{y'}=\varepsilon$ (Step 5); hence $h^\sharp_z=\varepsilon'\circ\pi$, i.e. $\varepsilon'^{-1}\circ h^\sharp_z=\pi$. So $h$ corresponds to the pair $(y,\pi)$ under the bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring] (b): $h=c\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\pi)$ is the morphism induced by $\mathcal O_{Y,y}=A\to A/J$.
